items.name: Move computer to OU
items.summary: Moves Active Directory computer objects to an OU chosen from the directory.
items.description: Moves the AD computer objects of one or more servers to an organizational unit browsed from the directory (Admin > Identity provider of type Active Directory). Runs over LDAP with a vault credential that has the right to move computer objects; no RSAT needed. Objects already in the OU are skipped; the previous OU of each object is reported so the move can be reverted.

inputs.name: ComputerNames
inputs.label: Computer names
inputs.help: One name per line (NetBIOS name or FQDN), max 200.

inputs.name: TargetOU
inputs.label: Target OU
inputs.help: OUs read from the directory (refreshed every 15 minutes).

inputs.name: DirectoryCredential
inputs.label: Directory credential
inputs.help: Account allowed to move computer objects between these OUs.

items.name: Agent baseline
items.summary: Install the approved agents of a software baseline set (monitoring, EDR, patching, backup) in a VM.
items.description: Runs inside the guest through VMware Tools (no WinRM / SSH). Installs only the packages of the set that are Approved in the software repository (Admin > Data files > software); Pending or Retired packages are skipped and listed in the result. Each package is verified before and after installation, so a re-run only installs what is missing.

inputs.name: VMName
inputs.label: Virtual machine
inputs.help: Powered-on VM with VMware Tools running.

inputs.name: BaselineSet
inputs.label: Baseline set
inputs.help: Must match the guest OS (Windows or Linux set).

inputs.name: GuestCredential
inputs.label: Guest administrator credential
inputs.help: Windows: local administrator (domain account to read UNC sources). Linux: root or a user with passwordless sudo.

items.name: AlmaLinux server baseline
items.summary: Join an AlmaLinux VM to Active Directory and apply NTP, sudo groups, extra packages and CIS basics.
items.description: Runs inside the guest through VMware Tools (no SSH). Installs the realmd/SSSD stack and chrony, configures NTP servers, joins the AD domain (password passed through stdin, never logged), permits the sudo groups and adds a validated sudoers drop-in, then applies CIS basics: network sysctl hardening, no root SSH login (checked with sshd -t), password minimum length 14, auditd and firewalld enabled (ssh kept open). Idempotent: safe to run again.

inputs.name: VMName
inputs.label: Virtual machine
inputs.help: Powered-on AlmaLinux VM with VMware Tools (open-vm-tools) running.

inputs.name: GuestCredential
inputs.label: Guest credential
inputs.help: root, or a user with passwordless sudo.

inputs.name: DomainName
inputs.label: AD domain
inputs.help: Required when joining.

inputs.name: DomainJoinCredential
inputs.label: Domain join account
inputs.help: Needed unless the VM is already joined.

inputs.name: SudoGroups
inputs.label: Sudo groups (comma separated)
inputs.help: AD groups allowed to log in and use sudo (no spaces in names).

inputs.name: NtpServers
inputs.label: NTP servers (comma separated)
inputs.help: Empty = keep the current chrony sources.

validation.patternMessage: Comma separated host names or IPv4 addresses.

inputs.name: ApplyCisBasics
inputs.label: Apply CIS basics
inputs.help: sysctl hardening, no root SSH login, password minlen 14, auditd, firewalld.

items.name: Aria Operations report
items.summary: Runs an Aria Operations report for a VM, host, cluster or datastore and attaches it to the request.
items.description: Generates one of the Aria Operations report definitions offered for the site (Admin > vCenter connections > Aria Operations) for the chosen object and attaches the PDF and / or CSV to the request. No change is made in vSphere.

items.name: Backup policy assignment
items.summary: Assign, change or remove the backup policy of a VM.
items.description: Tags the VM with its backup policy (vSphere tag category from Admin > Data files > Backup policies, tag = policy id). Backup products select their VMs by that tag, so the portal stays vendor-agnostic. Any previous policy is replaced; 'None' removes the VM from backup selection when that policy is defined in the data file.

inputs.name: Policy
inputs.label: Backup policy
inputs.help: Policies come from Admin > Data files > Backup policies. 'None' removes the VM from backup selection.

items.name: Three-tier application (WEB / APP / DB)
items.summary: Deploy a Windows web, application and database VM in one request, ready for the application team.
items.description: Creates <AppCode>WEB01 and <AppCode>APP01 on the selected workload cluster and <AppCode>DB01 on the database cluster (same datastore), keeps WEB and APP on different hosts (DRS anti-affinity), installs the software baseline, assigns the backup policy and optionally installs SQL Server on the DB VM (with data, log, backup and tempdb disks). Every step is reported; on failure everything created by the request is removed.

inputs.name: AppCode
inputs.label: Application code
inputs.help: VM names: <code>WEB01, <code>APP01, <code>DB01 (max 15 characters).

inputs.name: Workload
inputs.label: Workload cluster (WEB / APP tier)
inputs.help: Cluster for the web/app tier. The DB VM always goes to the database cluster.

inputs.name: Datastore
inputs.label: Datastore
inputs.help: Used by the three VMs: it must also be mounted on the DB cluster (checked before anything is created).

inputs.name: Size
inputs.label: Size
inputs.help: WEB and APP get this size; the DB VM gets the same vCPU and double memory.

inputs.name: DnsServers
inputs.label: DNS servers (comma separated)
inputs.help: Leave empty to use the site defaults.

inputs.name: GuestCredential
inputs.label: Guest administrator credential
inputs.help: Used inside the VMs for the software baseline and SQL Server setup.

inputs.name: InstallSql
inputs.label: Install SQL Server on the DB VM
inputs.help: Adds data, log, backup and tempdb disks to the DB VM and installs SQL Server 2022.

items.name: AWS cost report (idle resources)
items.summary: Find billable idle resources in AWS with a monthly list-price estimate.
items.description: Read-only report of unattached EBS volumes, unused Elastic IPs, instances stopped for a long time (EBS still billed) and snapshots older than 180 days, plus which resources carry the power schedule tag. Amounts are list-price estimates (USD, no discounts) to prioritise clean-up.

inputs.name: StoppedDaysThreshold

inputs.help: Instances / VMs powered off for fewer days are not reported.

items.description: Read-only report of unattached managed disks, unused public IPs, VMs stopped but not deallocated (compute still billed), long-deallocated VMs and snapshots older than 180 days, plus which resources carry the power schedule tag. Amounts are list-price estimates (USD, no discounts) to prioritise clean-up.

inputs.name: StoppedDaysThreshold
inputs.label: Stopped / deallocated for at least (days)
inputs.help: Instances / VMs powered off for fewer days are not reported.

items.name: AWS power action (by schedule tag)
items.summary: Start or stop every AWS instance whose PowerSchedule tag has a given value.
items.description: Selects resources by the power schedule tag (operations.powerSchedules.tagKey, default PowerSchedule) equal to the value you enter, e.g. office-hours, and starts or stops them (Stop-EC2Instance). Untagged resources are never touched. Runs as a dry run by default. Automatic scheduling is planned as future work.

inputs.name: TagValue
inputs.label: Power schedule tag value
inputs.help: Resources whose PowerSchedule tag equals this value (case-sensitive).

items.name: Azure power action (by schedule tag)
items.summary: Start or stop every Azure VM whose PowerSchedule tag has a given value.
items.description: Selects resources by the power schedule tag (operations.powerSchedules.tagKey, default PowerSchedule) equal to the value you enter, e.g. office-hours, and starts or stops them (Stop-AzVM (deallocate)). Untagged resources are never touched. Runs as a dry run by default. Automatic scheduling is planned as future work.

inputs.name: TagValue
inputs.label: Power schedule tag value
inputs.help: Resources whose PowerSchedule tag equals this value (case-sensitive).

items.name: New datastore (VMFS / NFS)
items.summary: Create a VMFS 6 or NFS datastore on every host of a cluster.
items.description: VMFS: formats a new LUN (visible on every host of the cluster and unused) as VMFS 6. NFS: mounts an NFS 3 / 4.1 export on every host. Optionally adds the datastore to an existing datastore cluster or creates a new one (Storage DRS manual). Rescans every host, holds the cluster storage lock while running and rolls back on failure. Submitting and approving require your password.

inputs.name: Cluster
inputs.label: Cluster
inputs.help: The datastore is created / mounted on every connected host of this cluster.

inputs.name: Lun
inputs.label: LUN (storage device)
inputs.help: Use 'Rescan storage' to discover new LUNs; every rescan asks for your password and is limited to one per cluster every 10 minutes.

inputs.name: NfsPath
inputs.label: NFS export path
inputs.help: The export must grant root access (no_root_squash / Root Access) to every host's VMkernel IP.

inputs.name: DatastoreName
inputs.label: Datastore name
inputs.help: 3-42 characters; must be unused in the vCenter.

validation.patternMessage: 3-42 characters: letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit.

inputs.name: DatastoreCluster
inputs.label: Add to datastore cluster
inputs.help: Optional. Leave empty for none. Only datastores of the same type can share a datastore cluster.

inputs.name: NewDatastoreCluster
inputs.label: Or create a new datastore cluster
inputs.help: Optional; Storage DRS in manual mode. Leave empty when you selected an existing datastore cluster.

items.name: Promote domain controller
items.summary: Promotes a domain-joined Windows VM to an additional domain controller, or checks its role.
items.description: High-impact change for Admins. Check mode reports the domain role. Promote mode verifies the VM is a member server of the same domain, takes a mandatory snapshot, installs AD DS, runs the prerequisite test and Install-ADDSDomainController (optionally with DNS), restarts the guest and verifies the role, the NTDS service and the SYSVOL / NETLOGON shares. Passwords (domain admin, DSRM) come from the vault and are never written in the guest. Requires approval, re-authentication and typing the VM name.

inputs.name: Domain
inputs.label: Domain
inputs.help: DNS name of the domain the VM is already joined to.

inputs.name: DomainCredential
inputs.label: Domain admin credential
inputs.help: Account allowed to add domain controllers; also used for the guest operations.

inputs.name: DsrmCredential
inputs.label: DSRM password
inputs.help: Vault entry whose password becomes the Directory Services Restore Mode password.

inputs.name: ConfirmVMName
inputs.label: Type the VM name to confirm

items.name: Distributed Port Group
items.summary: Create a VLAN-backed distributed port group on a vSphere Distributed Switch.
items.description: Creates a distributed port group with static (elastic) port binding on the selected VDS, sets the uplink load-balancing policy and the security policy. Pre-checks reject a name already used on any switch of the vCenter and a VLAN already used by another port group of the same switch. The port group is removed again if a later step fails.

inputs.name: VlanId
inputs.label: VLAN ID
inputs.help: Access VLAN 1-4094. Must not be used by another port group of the same switch.

inputs.name: Name
inputs.label: Port group name
inputs.help: Convention: PG-<SITE>-<VLAN>-<PURPOSE>, e.g. PG-DC1-120-APP. Must be unique in the vCenter.

inputs.name: Purpose
inputs.label: Purpose
inputs.help: Stored in the port group notes together with the change ticket.

inputs.name: NumPorts
inputs.label: Initial ports
inputs.help: Static binding with elastic allocation: the port count grows automatically.

options.label: Route based on originating virtual port (default)
Route based on physical NIC load
Route based on IP hash (requires LACP/EtherChannel)

inputs.name: SecurityPromiscuous
inputs.label: Allow promiscuous mode
inputs.help: Keep off unless an appliance (IDS, nested ESXi) requires it.

items.name: DRS Rule
items.summary: Create a DRS affinity / anti-affinity rule between VMs, or a VM-Host rule.
items.description: VM-VM rules keep VMs together (affinity) or apart (anti-affinity). VM-Host rules create or reuse the DRS groups '<rule>-vms' and '<rule>-hosts' and bind them with a must / should (not) run on rule. Pre-checks: every VM runs in the cluster, hosts belong to the cluster, the rule name is free, and no enabled rule of the opposite type already contains two or more of the same VMs.

options.label: VM-Host: must not run on hosts
VM-Host: should not run on hosts

inputs.name: RuleName
inputs.label: Rule name
inputs.help: Unique in the cluster. VM-Host rules also name the DRS groups <rule>-vms and <rule>-hosts.

inputs.name: VMNames
inputs.label: Virtual machines
inputs.help: One per line or comma separated. VM-VM rules need at least 2 VMs; all must run in the cluster.

inputs.name: HostNames
inputs.label: Hosts
inputs.help: Only for VM-Host rules (ignored for VM-VM). One per line or comma separated; FQDN or short name.

items.name: Initialize data disks
items.summary: Brings data disks online, frees the letter held by the CD-ROM and formats them with the requested letters.
items.description: On one or more Windows VMs: for each requested drive letter, takes the next disk without data partitions (disk-number order), brings it online, initializes it (GPT) when raw, creates the partition with the letter and formats it. A CD-ROM holding the letter is moved to a free letter. Letters already used by a data volume are skipped; disks with data partitions are never touched. Dry run (default) shows the plan only.

inputs.name: VMNames
inputs.label: Virtual machines
inputs.help: One VM name per line (or comma separated), max 50.

inputs.name: DriveLetters
inputs.label: Drive letters
inputs.help: In disk order, e.g. D or D,E,F,L,T.

inputs.name: Labels
inputs.label: Volume labels
inputs.help: Same order as the letters, e.g. Data,Logs. Empty = DataD, DataE...

inputs.name: AllocationUnit
inputs.label: Allocation unit
inputs.help: 64K is the usual choice for SQL Server data and log volumes.

inputs.name: MoveCdRom
inputs.label: Move CD-ROM off a requested letter

inputs.name: GuestCredential
inputs.label: Guest administrator credential
inputs.help: Local or domain administrator of the VMs.

items.name: Local admins & RDP users
items.summary: Adds accounts or groups to the local Administrators / Remote Desktop Users groups of Windows VMs.
items.description: Ensures the listed accounts or groups (DOMAIN\name or local names) are members of the local Administrators and / or Remote Desktop Users groups on one or more Windows VMs, through VMware Tools with a vault credential. Groups are addressed by well-known SID, so localized Windows works. Members already present are reported; nothing is removed. "Report only" lists what is missing without changing anything.

inputs.name: VMNames
inputs.label: Virtual machines
inputs.help: One VM name per line (or comma separated), max 50.

inputs.name: Accounts
inputs.label: Accounts or groups
inputs.help: One per line: DOMAIN\user, DOMAIN\group or a local account name.

inputs.name: GuestCredential
inputs.label: Guest administrator credential
inputs.help: Local or domain administrator of the VMs.

items.name: ESXi Host Maintenance Mode
items.summary: Put an ESXi host into maintenance mode (DRS evacuation) or take it out again.
items.description: Enter: checks N+1 memory capacity of the remaining hosts and that DRS is fully automated, then enters maintenance mode and lets DRS evacuate the VMs (vSAN: ensure accessibility). Exit: reconnects the host to the cluster. The VMs on the host, the re-authentication record and the reason are kept as evidence in the job log and the audit trail. Admin only.

inputs.name: EvacuatePoweredOff
inputs.label: Also move powered-off / suspended VMs
inputs.help: Powered-on VMs are always evacuated by DRS.

inputs.name: Reason
inputs.label: Reason
inputs.help: Kept as evidence in the audit trail.

items.name: Capacity forecast report
items.summary: Forecast datastore and cluster memory usage from the daily inventory history.
items.description: Fits a linear trend to the daily inventory samples (data/inventory/history) per datastore (used GB) and per cluster (VM memory vs physical memory, vCPU growth) and shows the days left before the threshold. Needs at least 7 daily samples; the portal records one per day at inventory refresh. Does not connect to vCenter.

inputs.name: ForecastDays
inputs.label: Forecast horizon (days)
inputs.help: Default from operations.capacity.forecastDays.

inputs.name: ThresholdPercent
inputs.label: Threshold (%)
inputs.help: Default from operations.capacity.thresholdPercent.

items.name: Certificate expiry report
items.summary: List the TLS certificates of vCenter, every ESXi host and extra endpoints with days to expiry.
items.description: Read-only. The portal server opens a TLS connection to vCenter, every ESXi host and the optional endpoints (port 443 unless given) and reads the presented certificate: subject, issuer, expiry, thumbprint. Status EXPIRING / CRITICAL / EXPIRED follows the warning days and operations.certificates.criticalDays; unreachable endpoints are listed as ERROR.

inputs.name: AdditionalEndpoints
inputs.label: Additional endpoints
inputs.help: One host or host:port per line (maximum 50). Port 443 when omitted.

inputs.name: WarningDays
inputs.label: Warn when expiring within (days)
inputs.help: Default from operations.certificates.warningDays.

items.name: Before / after change metrics
items.summary: Compares host storage latency, network usage and packet drops before and after a change.
items.description: Read-only. For every host of a cluster (or the hosts listed) compares a window before and a window after a change (MTU, firmware, multipathing, network): datastore read / write latency, device max latency (avg, p95, max), network usage, dropped and errored packets, from vCenter historical statistics. Each metric is marked improved, worse or unchanged at cluster and host level. Optionally lists the current iSCSI vmkernel MTU and session count.

inputs.name: HostNames
inputs.label: Hosts (optional)
inputs.help: Comma separated short or full host names; empty = every host of the cluster.

options.label: Same hours before and after the change

inputs.name: ChangeTime
inputs.label: Change time
inputs.help: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm in the portal time zone.

inputs.name: Hours
inputs.label: Hours before and after
inputs.help: Use windows with similar workload (e.g. 48 h = same weekdays). Max 168.

items.name: DRS rule compliance report
items.summary: Checks DRS VM-VM rules (existence, members, placement) and host memory over-commit for a cluster.
items.description: Read-only. Checks every VM-VM DRS rule of the cluster (enabled, placement: separate = one powered-on member per host, together = same host) and the expected rules listed for the cluster in the data file "Expected DRS rules" (exists, type, exact members). Adds host allocation (vRAM over-commit, memory used, vCPU:core, swap / balloon, large VMs per host), a VM detail table for VMs matching a name pattern (e.g. SQL), pending DRS recommendations and decommission candidates.

inputs.name: VmNamePattern
inputs.label: VM detail name pattern
inputs.help: Regular expression for the VM detail table (default from the data file, e.g. (?i)sql). Empty = data file value.

items.name: Hardening compliance report
items.summary: Check ESXi advanced settings, services, NTP and optionally VM settings against the hardening baseline.
items.description: Read-only assessment against Admin > Data files > Hardening baseline (ESXi advanced settings, services, NTP and VM advanced settings). Each check is PASS, FAIL or NOT SET (absent and the product default does not meet the control). Remediation will be a separate item that requires approval.

inputs.name: Cluster
inputs.label: Cluster
inputs.help: Leave empty to check every host of the site.

inputs.name: IncludeVms
inputs.label: Include VM advanced settings
inputs.help: Also checks the VM settings of the baseline for every VM in scope.

items.name: Orphaned VMDK assessment
items.summary: Finds virtual disks no registered VM references, classifies them and sizes the reclaimable capacity.
items.description: Read-only. Builds the list of files referenced by every registered VM and template in all enabled sites (so disks of VMs in another vCenter that shares a datastore are not reported), scans each datastore once and classifies the unreferenced disks: unregistered VM, detached disk, orphaned snapshot, CBT leftover, RDM mapping file. Reports capacity by category, age and datastore, the largest items and the full inventory. Nothing is deleted.

inputs.name: AllSites
inputs.label: Include every enabled site
inputs.help: Recommended: VMs registered in the other vCenters are taken into account and their datastores are scanned too.

inputs.name: DatastoreExcludePattern
inputs.label: Skip datastores matching
inputs.help: Regular expression on datastore names, e.g. ^local-|^datastore1

items.name: Version compliance report
items.summary: Compare vCenter, ESXi, VMware Tools and VM hardware versions with the approved baseline and advisories.
items.description: Read-only. Targets and security advisories come from Admin > Data files > Version baseline. Entities below a target or below the first fixed build of an advisory are NON-COMPLIANT; areas without a target show NOT SET. Produces an HTML report and one CSV per section.

items.name: vSphere health report
items.summary: Read-only health check of hosts, alarms, clusters, datastores, snapshots and VMware Tools.
items.description: Produces an HTML report and one CSV per section: host connection / maintenance / build / uptime, triggered alarms, cluster HA / DRS / EVC configuration, datastore free space against the site minimum, snapshots older than N days and VMware Tools issues. Optionally searches every datastore for orphaned VMDK files (slow). Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: IncludeOrphanedVmdk
inputs.label: Search for orphaned VMDK files
inputs.help: Browses every datastore; can take a long time on large sites. Results are candidates to review, never deleted.

items.name: Snapshot cleanup
items.summary: Find and remove expired or old VM snapshots across a datacenter.
items.description: Scans every VM of the site for snapshots matching the policy (portal snapshots with a passed 'Expires:' date, or snapshots older than the age limit), removes them and consolidates disks when vSphere flags it. Snapshots whose description marks them as protected (keep / do not delete / backup) are never touched. Dry run (default) only produces the report.

inputs.name: OlderThanDays
inputs.label: Older than (days)
inputs.help: Age limit for snapshots without an 'Expires:' stamp (or for all snapshots when 'Expired only' is off).

inputs.name: MinSizeGB
inputs.label: Minimum size (GB)
inputs.help: Ignore snapshots smaller than this. 0 = any size.

inputs.name: ExpiredOnly
inputs.label: Stamped snapshots: only when expired
inputs.help: Snapshots with an 'Expires: yyyy-MM-dd' stamp are removed only after that date. Unstamped snapshots use the age limit.

inputs.name: ChangeTicket
inputs.label: Change ticket
inputs.help: Required when Dry run is off.

items.name: Copy customization spec
items.summary: Copies an OS customization spec to another site and sets its passwords from the vault.
items.description: Clones an OS customization spec from the vCenter of one site to the vCenter of another (e.g. a new datacenter) and sets the local Administrator password, and optionally the domain join account, from vault entries (vCenter never exports them). An existing spec with the same name is replaced only with "Overwrite"; its previous settings are saved to the request.

inputs.name: AdminPassword
inputs.label: Local Administrator password
inputs.help: Vault entry whose password is set as the spec Administrator password.

items.name: SQL Server 2022 instance

inputs.name: GuestCredential
inputs.label: Guest administrator credential
inputs.help: Local administrator in the guest; a domain account is needed to read the media share.

inputs.name: InstanceName
inputs.label: Instance name
inputs.help: MSSQLSERVER = default instance.

validation.patternMessage: 1-16 characters, start with a letter; letters, digits and underscore.

inputs.name: SqlServiceCredential
inputs.label: Service account (optional)
inputs.help: Domain account for the Database Engine and Agent. Empty = virtual service accounts (NT Service\...).

inputs.name: MaxDop
inputs.label: MAXDOP
inputs.help: 0 = auto: number of vCPUs, max 8.

inputs.name: MaxServerMemoryMB

inputs.name: TempDbFiles

inputs.help: 0 = auto: number of vCPUs, max 8.

inputs.name: PrepareDisks
inputs.label: Prepare data disks (D, E, F, T)

items.name: Add disk to VM

items.name: Purge decommissioned VMs
items.summary: Permanently delete quarantined VMs whose quarantine period has ended.
items.description: Finds VMs in the quarantine folder that carry the decommission prefix, are powered off and whose 'Portal.Decommission' purge date has passed. Dry run (default) only produces the report; otherwise the VMs and their disks are deleted permanently.

items.name: Decommission VM (quarantine)
items.summary: Shut down, isolate and quarantine a VM before it is permanently deleted.
items.description: Nothing is deleted. The VM is shut down gracefully, renamed with the decommission prefix, its network adapters are disconnected, it is moved to the quarantine folder and its backup policy tag is removed. A 'Portal.Decommission' annotation records the request and the purge date; the 'Purge decommissioned VMs' item deletes it after the quarantine period. Restore = rename back and reconnect the adapters.

inputs.help: Application retired, replaced by..., owner confirmation. Kept in the job log.

items.name: Incident evidence export (RCA)
items.summary: Peak metrics, Aria alerts and vCenter events around an incident, packed for the ticket.
items.description: Exports the evidence of an incident for one VM and its host: Aria Operations statistics with the MAX rollup (peaks are kept), Aria alerts that overlap the window, vSphere performance counters, vCenter events and tasks (snapshots, vMotion, HA, power, connectivity) and current snapshots. Produces a summary HTML with timeline charts, CSV files and a zip evidence pack to attach to the incident or RCA. Read-only.

items.summary: Correlates guest OS, vSphere and Aria Operations data for one VM and ranks probable causes.

j.description: VMFS: formats a new LUN (visible on every host of the cluster and unused) as VMFS 6. NFS: mounts an NFS 3 / 4.1 export on every host. Optionally adds the datastore to an existing datastore cluster or creates a new one (Storage DRS manual). Rescans every host, holds the cluster storage lock while running and rolls back on failure. Submitting and approving require your password.

inputs.name: Cluster
inputs.label: Cluster
inputs.help: The datastore is created / mounted on every connected host of this cluster.

inputs.name: Lun
inputs.label: LUN (storage device)
inputs.help: Use 'Rescan storage' to discover new LUNs; every rescan asks for your password and is limited to one per cluster every 10 minutes.

inputs.name: NfsPath
inputs.label: NFS export path
inputs.help: The export must grant root access (no_root_squash / Root Access) to every host's VMkernel IP.

inputs.name: DatastoreName
inputs.label: Datastore name
inputs.help: 3-42 characters; must be unused in the vCenter.

validation.patternMessage: 3-42 characters: letters, digits, '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit.

inputs.name: DatastoreCluster
inputs.label: Add to datastore cluster
inputs.help: Optional. Leave empty for none. Only datastores of the same type can share a datastore cluster.

inputs.name: NewDatastoreCluster
inputs.label: Or create a new datastore cluster
inputs.help: Optional; Storage DRS in manual mode. Leave empty when you selected an existing datastore cluster.

j.name: Promote domain controller
j.summary: Promotes a domain-joined Windows VM to an additional domain controller, or checks its role.
j.description: High-impact change for Admins. Check mode reports the domain role. Promote mode verifies the VM is a member server of the same domain, takes a mandatory snapshot, installs AD DS, runs the prerequisite test and Install-ADDSDomainController (optionally with DNS), restarts the guest and verifies the role, the NTDS service and the SYSVOL / NETLOGON shares. Passwords (domain admin, DSRM) come from the vault and are never written in the guest. Requires approval, re-authentication and typing the VM name.

inputs.name: Domain
inputs.label: Domain
inputs.help: DNS name of the domain the VM is already joined to.

inputs.name: DomainCredential
inputs.label: Domain admin credential
inputs.help: Account allowed to add domain controllers; also used for the guest operations.

inputs.name: DsrmCredential
inputs.label: DSRM password
inputs.help: Vault entry whose password becomes the Directory Services Restore Mode password.

inputs.name: ConfirmVMName
inputs.label: Type the VM name to confirm

j.name: Distributed Port Group
j.summary: Create a VLAN-backed distributed port group on a vSphere Distributed Switch.
j.description: Creates a distributed port group with static (elastic) port binding on the selected VDS, sets the uplink load-balancing policy and the security policy. Pre-checks reject a name already used on any switch of the vCenter and a VLAN already used by another port group of the same switch. The port group is removed again if a later step fails.

inputs.name: VlanId
inputs.label: VLAN ID
inputs.help: Access VLAN 1-4094. Must not be used by another port group of the same switch.

inputs.name: Name
inputs.label: Port group name
inputs.help: Convention: PG-<SITE>-<VLAN>-<PURPOSE>, e.g. PG-DC1-120-APP. Must be unique in the vCenter.

inputs.name: Purpose
inputs.label: Purpose
inputs.help: Stored in the port group notes together with the change ticket.

inputs.name: NumPorts
inputs.label: Initial ports
inputs.help: Static binding with elastic allocation: the port count grows automatically.

options.label: Route based on originating virtual port (default)
Route based on physical NIC load
Route based on IP hash (requires LACP/EtherChannel)

inputs.name: SecurityPromiscuous
inputs.label: Allow promiscuous mode
inputs.help: Keep off unless an appliance (IDS, nested ESXi) requires it.

j.name: DRS Rule
j.summary: Create a DRS affinity / anti-affinity rule between VMs, or a VM-Host rule.
j.description: VM-VM rules keep VMs together (affinity) or apart (anti-affinity). VM-Host rules create or reuse the DRS groups '<rule>-vms' and '<rule>-hosts' and bind them with a must / should (not) run on rule. Pre-checks: every VM runs in the cluster, hosts belong to the cluster, the rule name is free, and no enabled rule of the opposite type already contains two or more of the same VMs.

options.label: VM-Host: must not run on hosts
VM-Host: should not run on hosts

inputs.name: RuleName
inputs.label: Rule name
inputs.help: Unique in the cluster. VM-Host rules also name the DRS groups <rule>-vms and <rule>-hosts.

inputs.name: VMNames
inputs.label: Virtual machines
inputs.help: One per line or comma separated. VM-VM rules need at least 2 VMs; all must run in the cluster.

inputs.name: HostNames
inputs.label: Hosts
inputs.help: Only for VM-Host rules (ignored for VM-VM). One per line or comma separated; FQDN or short name.

j.name: Initialize data disks
j.summary: Brings data disks online, frees the letter held by the CD-ROM and formats them with the requested letters.
j.description: On one or more Windows VMs: for each requested drive letter, takes the next disk without data partitions (disk-number order), brings it online, initializes it (GPT) when raw, creates the partition with the letter and formats it. A CD-ROM holding the letter is moved to a free letter. Letters already used by a data volume are skipped; disks with data partitions are never touched. Dry run (default) shows the plan only.

inputs.name: VMNames
inputs.label: Virtual machines
inputs.help: One VM name per line (or comma separated), max 50.

inputs.name: DriveLetters
inputs.label: Drive letters
inputs.help: In disk order, e.g. D or D,E,F,L,T.

validation.patternMessage: Letters D to Y separated by commas.

inputs.name: Labels
inputs.label: Volume labels
inputs.help: Same order as the letters, e.g. Data,Logs. Empty = DataD, DataE...

inputs.name: AllocationUnit
inputs.label: Allocation unit
inputs.help: 64K is the usual choice for SQL Server data and log volumes.

inputs.name: MoveCdRom
inputs.label: Move CD-ROM off a requested letter

inputs.name: GuestCredential
inputs.label: Guest administrator credential
inputs.help: Local or domain administrator of the VMs.

j.name: Local admins & RDP users
j.summary: Adds accounts or groups to the local Administrators / Remote Desktop Users groups of Windows VMs.
j.description: Ensures the listed accounts or groups (DOMAIN\name or local names) are members of the local Administrators and / or Remote Desktop Users groups on one or more Windows VMs, through VMware Tools with a vault credential. Groups are addressed by well-known SID, so localized Windows works. Members already present are reported; nothing is removed. "Report only" lists what is missing without changing anything.

inputs.name: VMNames
inputs.label: Virtual machines
inputs.help: One VM name per line (or comma separated), max 50.

inputs.name: Accounts
inputs.label: Accounts or groups
inputs.help: One per line: DOMAIN\user, DOMAIN\group or a local account name.

inputs.name: GuestCredential
inputs.label: Guest administrator credential
inputs.help: Local or domain administrator of the VMs.

j.name: ESXi Host Maintenance Mode
j.summary: Put an ESXi host into maintenance mode (DRS evacuation) or take it out again.
j.description: Enter: checks N+1 memory capacity of the remaining hosts and that DRS is fully automated, then enters maintenance mode and lets DRS evacuate the VMs (vSAN: ensure accessibility). Exit: reconnects the host to the cluster. The VMs on the host, the re-authentication record and the reason are kept as evidence in the job log and the audit trail. Admin only.

inputs.name: EvacuatePoweredOff
inputs.label: Also move powered-off / suspended VMs
inputs.help: Powered-on VMs are always evacuated by DRS.

inputs.name: Reason
inputs.label: Reason
inputs.help: Kept as evidence in the audit trail.

j.name: Capacity forecast report
j.summary: Forecast datastore and cluster memory usage from the daily inventory history.
j.description: Fits a linear trend to the daily inventory samples (data/inventory/history) per datastore (used GB) and per cluster (VM memory vs physical memory, vCPU growth) and shows the days left before the threshold. Needs at least 7 daily samples; the portal records one per day at inventory refresh. Does not connect to vCenter.

inputs.name: ForecastDays
inputs.label: Forecast horizon (days)
inputs.help: Default from operations.capacity.forecastDays.

inputs.name: ThresholdPercent
inputs.label: Threshold (%)
inputs.help: Default from operations.capacity.thresholdPercent.

j.name: Certificate expiry report
j.summary: List the TLS certificates of vCenter, every ESXi host and extra endpoints with days to expiry.
j.description: Read-only. The portal server opens a TLS connection to vCenter, every ESXi host and the optional endpoints (port 443 unless given) and reads the presented certificate: subject, issuer, expiry, thumbprint. Status EXPIRING / CRITICAL / EXPIRED follows the warning days and operations.certificates.criticalDays; unreachable endpoints are listed as ERROR.

inputs.name: AdditionalEndpoints
inputs.label: Additional endpoints
inputs.help: One host or host:port per line (maximum 50). Port 443 when omitted.

inputs.name: WarningDays
inputs.label: Warn when expiring within (days)
inputs.help: Default from operations.certificates.warningDays.

j.name: Before / after change metrics
j.summary: Compares host storage latency, network usage and packet drops before and after a change.
j.description: Read-only. For every host of a cluster (or the hosts listed) compares a window before and a window after a change (MTU, firmware, multipathing, network): datastore read / write latency, device max latency (avg, p95, max), network usage, dropped and errored packets, from vCenter historical statistics. Each metric is marked improved, worse or unchanged at cluster and host level. Optionally lists the current iSCSI vmkernel MTU and session count.

inputs.name: HostNames
inputs.label: Hosts (optional)
inputs.help: Comma separated short or full host names; empty = every host of the cluster.

options.label: Same hours before and after the change

inputs.name: ChangeTime
inputs.label: Change time
inputs.help: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm in the portal time zone.

inputs.name: Hours
inputs.label: Hours before and after
inputs.help: Use windows with similar workload (e.g. 48 h = same weekdays). Max 168.

j.name: DRS rule compliance report
j.summary: Checks DRS VM-VM rules (existence, members, placement) and host memory over-commit for a cluster.
j.description: Read-only. Checks every VM-VM DRS rule of the cluster (enabled, placement: separate = one powered-on member per host, together = same host) and the expected rules listed for the cluster in the data file "Expected DRS rules" (exists, type, exact members). Adds host allocation (vRAM over-commit, memory used, vCPU:core, swap / balloon, large VMs per host), a VM detail table for VMs matching a name pattern (e.g. SQL), pending DRS recommendations and decommission candidates.

inputs.name: VmNamePattern
inputs.label: VM detail name pattern
inputs.help: Regular expression for the VM detail table (default from the data file, e.g. (?i)sql). Empty = data file value.

j.name: Hardening compliance report
j.summary: Check ESXi advanced settings, services, NTP and optionally VM settings against the hardening baseline.
j.description: Read-only assessment against Admin > Data files > Hardening baseline (ESXi advanced settings, services, NTP and VM advanced settings). Each check is PASS, FAIL or NOT SET (absent and the product default does not meet the control). Remediation will be a separate item that requires approval.

inputs.name: Cluster
inputs.label: Cluster
inputs.help: Leave empty to check every host of the site.

inputs.name: IncludeVms
inputs.label: Include VM advanced settings
inputs.help: Also checks the VM settings of the baseline for every VM in scope.

j.name: Orphaned VMDK assessment
j.summary: Finds virtual disks no registered VM references, classifies them and sizes the reclaimable capacity.
j.description: Read-only. Builds the list of files referenced by every registered VM and template in all enabled sites (so disks of VMs in another vCenter that shares a datastore are not reported), scans each datastore once and classifies the unreferenced disks: unregistered VM, detached disk, orphaned snapshot, CBT leftover, RDM mapping file. Reports capacity by category, age and datastore, the largest items and the full inventory. Nothing is deleted.

inputs.name: AllSites
inputs.label: Include every enabled site
inputs.help: Recommended: VMs registered in the other vCenters are taken into account and their datastores are scanned too.

inputs.name: DatastoreExcludePattern
inputs.label: Skip datastores matching
inputs.help: Regular expression on datastore names, e.g. ^local-|^datastore1

j.name: Version compliance report
j.summary: Compare vCenter, ESXi, VMware Tools and VM hardware versions with the approved baseline and advisories.
j.description: Read-only. Targets and security advisories come from Admin > Data files > Version baseline. Entities below a target or below the first fixed build of an advisory are NON-COMPLIANT; areas without a target show NOT SET. Produces an HTML report and one CSV per section.

j.name: vSphere health report
j.summary: Read-only health check of hosts, alarms, clusters, datastores, snapshots and VMware Tools.
j.description: Produces an HTML report and one CSV per section: host connection / maintenance / build / uptime, triggered alarms, cluster HA / DRS / EVC configuration, datastore free space against the site minimum, snapshots older than N days and VMware Tools issues. Optionally searches every datastore for orphaned VMDK files (slow). Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: IncludeOrphanedVmdk
inputs.label: Search for orphaned VMDK files
inputs.help: Browses every datastore; can take a long time on large sites. Results are candidates to review, never deleted.

j.name: Snapshot cleanup
j.summary: Find and remove expired or old VM snapshots across a datacenter.
j.description: Scans every VM of the site for snapshots matching the policy (portal snapshots with a passed 'Expires:' date, or snapshots older than the age limit), removes them and consolidates disks when vSphere flags it. Snapshots whose description marks them as protected (keep / do not delete / backup) are never touched. Dry run (default) only produces the report.

inputs.name: OlderThanDays
inputs.label: Older than (days)
inputs.help: Age limit for snapshots without an 'Expires:' stamp (or for all snapshots when 'Expired only' is off).

inputs.name: MinSizeGB
inputs.label: Minimum size (GB)
inputs.help: Ignore snapshots smaller than this. 0 = any size.

inputs.name: ExpiredOnly
inputs.label: Stamped snapshots: only when expired
inputs.help: Snapshots with an 'Expires: yyyy-MM-dd' stamp are removed only after that date. Unstamped snapshots use the age limit.

inputs.name: ChangeTicket
inputs.label: Change ticket
inputs.help: Required when Dry run is off.

j.name: Copy customization spec
j.summary: Copies an OS customization spec to another site and sets its passwords from the vault.
j.description: Clones an OS customization spec from the vCenter of one site to the vCenter of another (e.g. a new datacenter) and sets the local Administrator password, and optionally the domain join account, from vault entries (vCenter never exports them). An existing spec with the same name is replaced only with "Overwrite"; its previous settings are saved to the request.

inputs.name: AdminPassword
inputs.label: Local Administrator password
inputs.help: Vault entry whose password is set as the spec Administrator password.

j.name: SQL Server 2022 instance
j.summary: Install a SQL Server 2022 Database Engine instance on an existing Windows Server VM.
j.description: Runs inside the guest through VMware Tools (no WinRM). Optionally prepares four RAW disks as D: data, E: logs, F: backup and T: tempdb (NTFS, 64 KB allocation unit, in disk-number order), installs the Database Engine unattended from the site media share, then sets max server memory, MAXDOP, cost threshold for parallelism 50 and backup compression. The guest account must be able to read the media share (domain account) and is added as sysadmin for the post-configuration.

inputs.name: VMName
inputs.label: Virtual machine
inputs.help: Powered-on Windows Server VM with VMware Tools running.

inputs.name: GuestCredential
inputs.label: Guest administrator credential
inputs.help: Local administrator in the guest; a domain account is needed to read the media share.

inputs.name: InstanceName
inputs.label: Instance name
inputs.help: MSSQLSERVER = default instance.

validation.patternMessage: 1-16 characters, start with a letter; letters, digits and underscore.

inputs.name: SqlServiceCredential
inputs.label: Service account (optional)
inputs.help: Domain account for the Database Engine and Agent. Empty = virtual service accounts (NT Service\...).

inputs.name: MaxDop
inputs.label: MAXDOP
inputs.help: 0 = auto: number of vCPUs, max 8.

inputs.name: MaxServerMemoryMB
inputs.label: Max server memory (MB)
inputs.help: 0 = auto: VM memory minus max(4 GB, 10%).

inputs.name: TempDbFiles
inputs.label: tempdb data files
inputs.help: 0 = auto: number of vCPUs, max 8.

inputs.name: PrepareDisks
inputs.label: Prepare data disks (D, E, F, T)
inputs.help: Formats the first 4 RAW disks (by disk number) as D: data, E: logs, F: backup, T: tempdb. Off = the drives must already exist.

j.name: Add disk to VM
j.summary: Hot-add a thin-provisioned data disk to an existing VM.
j.description: Adds a virtual disk on the VM's datastore, respecting the site free-space floor. The guest OS must bring the disk online.

j.name: AlmaLinux VM
j.summary: Deploy a new AlmaLinux virtual machine on vSphere from the golden template.
j.description: Clones the approved AlmaLinux template of the selected datacenter, applies Linux guest customization (hostname, domain, network), places it on the APP or DB cluster, sizes CPU/memory, adds an optional data disk and powers on the VM. Standard sizes run without approval.

inputs.name: VMName
inputs.label: VM name
inputs.help: Hostname: max 15 characters, letters, digits and hyphens.

validation.patternMessage: 3-15 characters, must start with a letter; letters, digits and hyphens only.

inputs.name: Workload
inputs.label: Workload type
inputs.help: APP deploys to the application cluster, DB to the database cluster of the selected datacenter.

inputs.name: AdditionalDiskGB
inputs.label: Additional data disk (GB)
inputs.help: 0 = no additional disk. Thin provisioned.

inputs.name: DnsServers
inputs.label: DNS servers (comma separated)
inputs.help: Leave empty to use the site defaults.

inputs.name: NoteApplication
inputs.label: Application / service
inputs.help: Business application hosted on the VM.

inputs.name: NoteExpiration
inputs.label: Expiration / review date
inputs.help: YYYY-MM-DD, empty = permanent

j.name: Purge decommissioned VMs
j.summary: Permanently delete quarantined VMs whose quarantine period has ended.
j.description: Finds VMs in the quarantine folder that carry the decommission prefix, are powered off and whose 'Portal.Decommission' purge date has passed. Dry run (default) only produces the report; otherwise the VMs and their disks are deleted permanently.

inputs.name: ChangeTicket
inputs.label: Change ticket
inputs.help: Required when Dry run is off.

j.name: Decommission VM (quarantine)
j.summary: Shut down, isolate and quarantine a VM before it is permanently deleted.
j.description: Nothing is deleted. The VM is shut down gracefully, renamed with the decommission prefix, its network adapters are disconnected, it is moved to the quarantine folder and its backup policy tag is removed. A 'Portal.Decommission' annotation records the request and the purge date; the 'Purge decommissioned VMs' item deletes it after the quarantine period. Restore = rename back and reconnect the adapters.

inputs.name: Reason
inputs.label: Reason for decommission
inputs.help: Application retired, replaced by..., owner confirmation. Kept in the job log.

inputs.name: ConfirmName
inputs.label: Type the VM name to confirm
inputs.help: Must match the selected VM name exactly (case-insensitive).

j.name: Incident evidence export (RCA)
j.summary: Peak metrics, Aria alerts and vCenter events around an incident, packed for the ticket.
j.description: Exports the evidence of an incident for one VM and its host: Aria Operations statistics with the MAX rollup (peaks are kept), Aria alerts that overlap the window, vSphere performance counters, vCenter events and tasks (snapshots, vMotion, HA, power, connectivity) and current snapshots. Produces a summary HTML with timeline charts, CSV files and a zip evidence pack to attach to the incident or RCA. Read-only.

inputs.name: IncidentTime
inputs.label: Incident time
inputs.help: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm in the portal time zone (operations.troubleshooting.timeZone, default UTC).

inputs.name: UseAria
inputs.label: Include Aria Operations
inputs.help: Used when the site has an Aria Operations connection.

j.name: Move VMs to folder
j.summary: Files VMs under a vCenter VM folder (inventory only, no downtime).
j.description: Moves one or more VMs into a VM folder chosen from the site inventory. Only the inventory location changes: no vMotion, no downtime. VMs already in the folder are skipped.

inputs.name: VMNames
inputs.label: Virtual machines
inputs.help: One VM name per line (or comma separated), max 200.

j.name: VM power action
j.summary: Power on, shut down, restart or reset one or more VMs.
j.description: Power operations on an existing VM. Shutdown and restart are graceful (VMware Tools); Reset is a hard reset. Several VMs can be listed in "Additional VMs"; each one is processed and reported. A guest restart can fall back to a hard reset when VMware Tools is not running.

inputs.name: AdditionalVMs
inputs.label: Additional VMs (optional)
inputs.help: More VM names, one per line (max 50 in total).

inputs.name: ResetIfToolsDown
inputs.label: Hard reset if Tools are not running

j.name: Resize VM (CPU / memory)
j.summary: Change vCPU and memory of an existing VM.
j.description: Uses hot-add when enabled on the VM. For decreases or when hot-add is disabled, the VM is shut down gracefully, resized and started again only if you allow a power cycle.

inputs.name: AllowPowerCycle
inputs.label: Allow power cycle if hot-add is not possible

j.name: VM right-sizing report
j.summary: Advisory vCPU / memory recommendations from vCenter performance history.
j.description: Reads CPU and memory usage history from vCenter (average and 95th percentile) for one VM or every powered-on VM of a cluster (max 200) and flags oversized (WARN) and undersized (FAIL) VMs with a recommended size. Nothing is changed; apply a recommendation with the 'Resize VM' item.

inputs.name: VMName
inputs.label: Virtual machine (optional)
inputs.help: Leave empty to analyse every powered-on VM of the cluster (max 200).

inputs.name: LookbackDays
inputs.label: Look back (days)
inputs.help: Up to 30 days uses 2-hour samples; longer periods use daily samples.

j.name: VM Snapshot (pre-change)
j.summary: Take a point-in-time snapshot of an existing VM before a change window.
j.description: Creates a vSphere snapshot of the selected VM with an expiry date stamped in the description. Snapshots are operational safety nets, not backups; the expiry drives the snapshot cleanup policy.

inputs.name: RetentionDays
inputs.label: Retention (days)
inputs.help: Maximum 7 days per snapshot policy.

j.name: Isolated test clone
j.summary: Clone a VM onto an isolated network for testing (patches, upgrades, restores).
j.description: Full clone of the selected VM on the same host, placed in the test-clones folder. Every network adapter is moved to the isolated port group and gets a new manual MAC address, so the clone can run next to the original without conflicts. The clone carries a 'Portal.TestClone' annotation with its expiry date.

inputs.name: CloneName
inputs.label: Clone name
inputs.help: Leave empty for the test-clone prefix + source name (e.g. TST-APP01).

validation.patternMessage: Letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen; 2-80 characters.

inputs.name: IsolatedPortGroup
inputs.label: Isolated port group
inputs.help: Must be an isolated network without uplinks. When the portal defines an isolated port group, only that one is accepted.

inputs.name: Datastore
inputs.label: Datastore
inputs.help: Must be visible to the source VM's host.

inputs.name: DaysToKeep
inputs.label: Keep for (days)
inputs.help: Maximum 7 days per test-clone policy.

j.name: VM troubleshooting
j.summary: Correlates guest OS, vSphere and Aria Operations data for one VM and ranks probable causes.
j.description: Read-only diagnosis of one VM over a time window (last hour / day / week, or around an incident). Collects vSphere performance counters of the VM and its host (CPU ready, co-stop, balloon, swap, disk latency, network drops), snapshots, VMware Tools and vCenter events; optionally runs a read-only script in the guest (uptime, pending reboot, memory, disks, stopped services, error events) and reads Aria Operations (health, alerts, peak statistics). Returns a verdict, ranked findings with their sources, an HTML report with charts and an evidence pack (zip). Nothing is changed.

inputs.name: VMName
inputs.label: Virtual machine
inputs.help: Search the inventory by name.

inputs.name: IncidentTime
inputs.label: Incident time
inputs.help: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm in the portal time zone (operations.troubleshooting.timeZone, default UTC).

inputs.name: IncludeHost
inputs.label: Include host and datastores
inputs.help: Adds host counters and events to tell VM problems from host / datastore problems.

inputs.name: UseGuest
inputs.label: Include guest OS
inputs.help: Runs a read-only script through VMware Tools with a vault credential.

inputs.name: GuestCredential
inputs.label: Guest credential
inputs.help: Windows: local or domain administrator. Linux: a user that can read the journal (root or sudo).

inputs.name: UseAria
inputs.label: Include Aria Operations
inputs.help: Used when the site has an Aria Operations connection (Admin > vCenter connections).

inputs.name: AriaReport
inputs.label: Also generate Aria report (PDF)
inputs.help: Report definitions offered by the Admin for this site.

j.name: VM Migration (vMotion)
j.summary: Move a VM to another cluster of the same datacenter, optionally to another datastore.
j.description: Live-migrates the VM (vMotion / cross-cluster, optionally with Storage vMotion) to the connected host of the target cluster with the lowest memory usage. Pre-checks: EVC compatibility, port groups available on the target hosts, datastore free-space floor of the site and memory headroom of the target cluster. Runs as soon as it is approved; a scheduled migration window is planned for a later version.

inputs.name: TargetDatastore
inputs.label: Target datastore
inputs.help: Leave empty to keep the current datastore (it must be shared with the target cluster).

inputs.name: KeepPortGroups
inputs.label: Keep port groups (check every target host)
inputs.help: The VM keeps its networks. On: every connected target host must have them (DRS can move the VM later). Off: only the destination host is checked.

j.name: Windows Server 2025 VM
j.summary: Deploy a new Windows Server 2025 virtual machine on vSphere from the golden template.
j.description: Clones the approved Windows Server 2025 template of the selected datacenter, applies guest customization (hostname, network), places it on the APP or DB cluster, sizes CPU/memory, adds an optional data disk and powers on the VM. DNS registration follows your change process.

inputs.name: VMName
inputs.label: VM name
inputs.help: NetBIOS compatible: max 15 characters, letters, digits and hyphens.

validation.patternMessage: 3-15 characters, must start with a letter; letters, digits and hyphens only.

inputs.name: Workload
inputs.label: Workload type
inputs.help: APP deploys to the application cluster, DB to the database cluster of the selected datacenter.

inputs.name: AdditionalDiskGB
inputs.label: Additional data disk (GB)
inputs.help: 0 = no additional disk. Thin provisioned.

inputs.name: DnsServers
inputs.label: DNS servers (comma separated)
inputs.help: Leave empty to use the site defaults.

inputs.name: NoteApplication
inputs.label: Application / service
inputs.help: Business application hosted on the VM.

inputs.name: NoteExpiration
inputs.label: Expiration / review date
inputs.help: YYYY-MM-DD, empty = permanent

j.name: Windows VM build (batch, bootstrap)
j.summary: Builds one or many Windows VMs from a CSV list, with in-guest bootstrap, validation and a closure report.
j.description: Clones every VM of the list from the site Windows template with the site customization spec (CPU, memory, portgroup, primary disk, extra disks, VM notes), then runs a portal-driven bootstrap through VMware Tools: static IP, rename, Windows Update rounds, activation, firewall / RDP, recovery partition and C: extension, data disks with the requested letters, CD-ROM letter, domain join and local groups. No password is written in the guest. Each VM is validated read-only and a closure report with ticket text is attached. Profile Citrix skips Windows Update, activation and firewall. Use "Validate only" to check the list first.

inputs.name: Folder
inputs.label: VM folder (optional)
inputs.help: Empty = site default folder.

j.name: Windows roles and features
j.summary: Install a standard Windows Server role bundle (IIS, .NET, Failover Clustering, File Server) or configure MSDTC.
j.description: Runs inside the guest through VMware Tools (no WinRM). Feature bundles are installed with Install-WindowsFeature (idempotent). MSDTC configures the local DTC network access, inbound/outbound transactions and authentication, enables the Distributed Transaction Coordinator firewall rules, restarts the service and verifies the settings (a clustered DTC role is not configured). The VM is restarted only when needed and allowed.
